title: BYD HAN 2026: export evidence before payment
text: Export evidence check BYD HAN 2026: export evidence before payment Assess the BYD HAN as a named European specification, then verify the VIN, market documents and destination rules before paying. AI policy · Source methodology What the evidence actually covers BYD Europe presents the HAN as a pure-electric flagship sedan with dual-motor all-wheel drive, Blade Battery technology, a heat pump and Vehicle-to-Load. Its European brochure lists 380 kW peak power, 3.9 seconds from 0 to 100 km/h, 180 km/h and 410 litres of cargo capacity. These are useful reference points for the cited European specification, not a global 2026 specification. A seller should identify the country of origin, trim, build date, type code and VIN before any comparison becomes a buying decision. The brochure also lists up to 521 km WLTP combined. WLTP is a named laboratory procedure; traffic, temperature, road speed, payload, tyres, heating and air conditioning can change the distance achieved. The BYD Europe page itself warns that actual range and consumption depend on use. Treat 521 km as evidence about a test configuration, not as a delivery promise, and request the dated local data sheet for the car being offered. Configuration and market boundary HAN is a model name used across markets, while the cited evidence is European. A China-market, Gulf-market or parallel-import car may differ in battery documentation, charging hardware, connectivity, language, driver-assistance calibration, steering side, lighting and available service channels. None of those differences can be resolved from the model badge. Ask for VIN decoding, the original certificate of conformity or equivalent, the full equipment list and photographs of the charging port and identification plates. Do not combine a headline number from one country with a trim or battery from another. The Spain page shows why a local market page matters: specifications are presented within a local product and sales context. The existence of a European brochure does not establish that a non-European car carries the same equipment, software or approval basis. A dated quotation should identify currency, tax treatment, shipping term and the exact vehicle rather than merely saying HAN 2026. Safety, approval and support This record does not attach an independent crash score to the exact HAN configuration. Safety equipment named in a brochure is not the same as a current test result, and a result for one market or model year should not be transferred to another VIN without evidence. For destination registration, ask the authority or an experienced homologation agent which documents, lighting, communications, braking, emissions or electric-vehicle requirements apply. UNECE regulatory context is a starting point, not approval for a particular country. Support needs the same discipline. Confirm whether the destination has an authorized service route for this VIN, whether diagnostic software and parts are available, and where battery and high-voltage work would be performed. This record makes no claim about warranty territory, roadside assistance, recall coverage or repair pricing. Get those terms in writing from the responsible market channel, and check recall status with the vehicle identifier rather than relying on a seller's general statement. Charging and daily export use The European description of the HAN includes V2L and a heat pump, but the buyer still needs the exact charging specification. Confirm AC and DC limits, connector standard, cable supply, onboard software, navigation region and whether local public networks recognize the car. A vehicle can be physically capable of charging while remaining inconvenient to operate if its connector, account system or communications services are not supported at the destination. Range planning should use the destination climate and route, not only WLTP. A heavy sedan travelling quickly in heat or cold can use materially more energy than a laboratory cycle suggests; auxiliary loads and tyre condition matter too. Before shipment, record the battery state of health if the vehicle is used, the charging test result, odometer, tyre condition and any warning messages. These checks are evidence about the actual unit, not assumptions about all HAN cars. Landed-cost decision record A credible landed-cost comparison starts with a dated vehicle quotation and then adds export handling, freight, insurance, destination duty, VAT or sales tax, port charges, registration, inspection, homologation, charging adaptation and a contingency for parts or software work. No universal HAN price is stated here because country, tax, trim, new or used status and seller terms change the result. A low origin price is not proof of a low registered cost. The purchase file should contain the VIN, invoice, bill of lading, packing or transport record, conformity documents, battery information, service terms, import classification and destination approval decision. Stop when a seller cannot identify the exact specification or asks the buyer to infer warranty and registration from a European web page. The evidence supports a careful comparison, not a claim that any HAN is currently available, approved or economically suitable in every market. Frequently asked questions Is 521 km the real range of every 2026 HAN? No. It is a cited European WLTP combined result for a named configuration. Weather, speed, payload, heating, air conditioning and other conditions affect real use. Can a European HAN brochure approve an imported car? No. It identifies a European specification. The destination authority must decide whether the exact VIN and documents meet local registration and approval rules. What should I request from an exporter? Request VIN, build date, type code, local data sheet, equipment list, battery and charging details, conformity documents, dated quotation and written service or warranty territory. Does this record establish price or availability? No. It establishes no universal price, stock position, warranty, recall status or delivery promise. Those items need a dated offer and checks for the destination market. title: BYD SEAL Export Buyer Guide: Which Version Are You Actually Buying?
text: Configuration-matched export research BYD SEAL Export Buyer Guide: Which Version Are You Actually Buying? BYD SEAL export guide using the current UK 2026 specification as a controlled reference. Compare Design and Excellence AWD, charging, safety scope, software and destination compatibility before buying. User 3204 · CC BY-SA 4.0 By AutoBridge Export Editorial Team Review Human review recorded · 2026-08-30 Method Document research and vehicle comparison Evidence Documented public and primary sources; no first-hand claim AI assisted research organization, drafting or translation; sources and claims remain subject to the stated review process. AI policy · Source methodology Use “2026” only where the source proves it BYD UK currently markets a BYD SEAL 2026 with Design and Excellence AWD versions. This is strong evidence for the UK market; it is not proof that every SEAL offered from China or another country is the same 2026 specification. For export purchasing, start with VIN, build date, original market and exact trim. Keep the current UK specification as a comparison reference, not a global specification sheet. The two UK reference versions have materially different performance BYD UK lists the Design with 354 miles WLTP combined range, rear-wheel drive and 0–62 mph in 5. 9 seconds. Excellence AWD is listed with 323 miles WLTP, all-wheel drive, 0–62 mph in 3. 8 seconds and 390 kW/530 PS. The current UK leaflet identifies the Blade Battery as LFP and lists 82. 5 kWh for both reference versions. A buyer should not combine the Design range with the Excellence performance and present that as one vehicle. Charging and luggage figures must stay attached to the reference market BYD UK states AC charging at 11 kW and DC fast charging up to 150 kW, with charging-time claims made under specified conditions. The current UK material also presents a 485 L rear boot and 72 L front boot. Charging speed varies with charger voltage/power, battery temperature and state of charge. Before export, verify the actual charging inlet, onboard charger and software of the VIN, as another market may use a different configuration or service environment. Safety ratings have their own scope Euro NCAP assessed the BYD SEAL in 2023, and ANCAP states that its rating applies to BYD SEAL variants within the technical-report scope for Australia/New Zealand. Those independent assessments are useful evidence, but the buyer should record the rating year and applicable variants instead of simply writing “five-star globally. ” For the exact export vehicle, verify airbag/ADAS specification, production period and whether the independent rating applies to that version. Connected features can become an export problem The UK leaflet notes that navigation is not available in all languages or countries and tells customers to check local availability. That warning is directly relevant to parallel exports. App services, OTA updates, embedded connectivity, voice control, navigation and online accounts can depend on region. Before payment, test or obtain written evidence for the destination language, smartphone integration, app registration, OTA pathway, charging-map dependence and any subscription that matters to the customer. Buyer decision The SEAL can be a strong electric-saloon option, but the purchase should be tied to a specific version. Before payment verify VIN, original market, battery and motor configuration, charging inlet/power, WLTP claim source, safety-rating scope, warranty region, software/services, tyre specification, parts and diagnostic support. Do not publish a single “global 2026 BYD SEAL specification. ” The safe approach is to show a clearly labelled market reference and then verify the offered vehicle against it. What the quotation and contract should identify A strong SEAL quotation should identify the VIN or, before VIN allocation, a frozen market-specific configuration that will later be reconciled to the VIN. Record original market, production date, trim, driven wheels, battery, official range test cycle, AC and DC charging hardware, wheel and tyre package and the equipment that materially affects the buyer’s decision. If the seller is quoting the UK MY26 reference, the contract should not quietly combine Design and Excellence AWD values: the Design reference carries the longer WLTP range and RWD performance figures, while Excellence AWD carries the quicker acceleration and AWD output. Once a specific export vehicle is allocated, photograph its VIN, labels, charge inlet, wheels, dashboard and key option areas and compare them against the contractual configuration. The after-sales file matters as much as the specification sheet. Confirm which warranty region applies, whether the destination has authorised or competent high-voltage diagnosis, what charging cable is supplied and whether navigation, app functions, cellular services and OTA support are available in that market. Safety evidence should identify the exact Euro NCAP or ANCAP assessment scope being referenced rather than displaying a generic “five-star” badge. For a parallel import, connected functions may depend on region, account, SIM/network or software support. These items should be treated as conditional until written destination evidence exists. A buyer who needs fleet uptime should also identify collision parts, windscreen/ADAS calibration, tyres and battery/inverter service routes before shipment. When the BYD SEAL evidence is not strong enough Do not approve payment when the quotation mixes data from different trims or countries. A common error is to pair the UK Design range number with the Excellence AWD acceleration or power figure and present the result as one vehicle. Another is to treat “2026” in a current UK leaflet as proof that every SEAL in every source market is the same model-year configuration. The vehicle identity must come first; the reference brochure comes second. Also pause when the seller cannot show the actual charge port or refuses to state whether the offered unit is RWD or AWD, when a safety rating is described as global, or when app, OTA and warranty coverage are promised without destination support. A model-family photograph or a public specification page can help identify what should be checked, but it does not prove the exact unit. The purchase is ready only when VIN-level evidence, market-specific specifications, safety scope and service assumptions no longer contradict one another. Frequently asked questions BYD SEAL: Is this a universal 2026 specification? No. The cited facts belong to named markets and configurations; match model code, build date, drivetrain, equipment and VIN. Output and driveline: Design 230 kW RWD; Excellence 390 kW AWD; output changes with engine, motor, fuel, software and driveline. BYD SEAL: Which identity evidence should be obtained before a deposit? Obtain VIN and certification-label photographs, a dated configuration sheet, ownership status, inspection evidence and a quotation that identifies the same vehicle. Energy, fuel or charging: Blade Battery 82. 5 kWh; AC 11 kW; DC 150 kW; verify the exact fuel grade, battery, inlet and test method. BYD SEAL: Does the cited safety result approve the import? No. Confirm that the rating covers the body, drivetrain, steering side and production range, then obtain destination registration approval separately. Capacity and working limit: 5; 400 L + 53 L; use the certification and load labels on the physical vehicle. BYD SEAL: What operating compatibility needs checking? Verify fuel or charging hardware, local energy supply, tyres, payload or seating needs, diagnostics, software, parts and recall support. Independent safety scope: Euro NCAP 2023: Design RWD / Excellence AWD; ANCAP 2023; apply only to the listed body, drivetrain and production range. BYD SEAL: How should total landed cost be compared? Use one scope and Incoterm, then include inspection, transport, freight, insurance, duty, tax, adaptation, registration, service and foreseeable downtime. Market compatibility: LHD / RHD; CCS2; OTA; eCall; destination approval, warranty and availability require written confirmation. title: BYD SONG PLUS DM-i 2026: What Overseas Buyers Should Verify
text: Configuration-matched export research BYD SONG PLUS DM-i 2026: What Overseas Buyers Should Verify BYD Mexico currently markets the SONG PLUS DM-i as a 2026 model, but BYD pages in the Middle East & Africa and the Caribbean list SONG PLUS DM-i without establishing one globally identical 2026 specification. The Caribbean site also offers both LHD and RHD versions. For an export buyer, that means the model name is only the starting point. User 3204 · CC BY-SA 4.0 By AutoBridge Export Editorial Team Review Human review recorded · 2026-08-29 Method Document research and vehicle comparison Evidence Documented public and primary sources; no first-hand claim AI assisted research organization, drafting or translation; sources and claims remain subject to the stated review process. AI policy · Source methodology The 2026 badge is not a universal global specification Before comparing price or equipment, identify the exact VIN, build date, steering side, sales market, trim and the official specification sheet that belongs to that vehicle. Keep the existing 2026 URL for search continuity, but do not describe every SONG PLUS DM-i offered worldwide as one universal 2026 configuration. Use published specifications as market-bound reference data A recent official BYD Chile specification sheet provides one useful reference configuration: five seats, 4,705 mm length, 1,890 mm width, 1,670 mm height and a 2,765 mm wheelbase. It lists front-wheel drive, a 1.5-litre turbo petrol engine rated at 96 kW and 220 N·m, a front electric motor rated at 150 kW and 300 N·m, and an 18.3 kWh Blade LFP battery. The same sheet lists 105 km of EV range and 1,105 km total range under NEDC, Type 2 AC charging up to 5.6 kW, a 0–100 km/h time of 8.3 seconds, 235/50 R19 tyres, 552 litres of cargo capacity and a 1,900 kg kerb weight. BYD Mexico also currently advertises the 2026 SONG PLUS DM-i with NEDC figures and a 5.1 L/100 km low-fuel-consumption headline. Those figures are valuable for comparison, but they are not a promise that a vehicle sourced from another market has the same battery, charging hardware, curb weight, software or equipment. Put the quotation beside the market-specific official sheet and match line by line. The PHEV advantage depends on how the vehicle will actually be used The SONG PLUS DM-i is a plug-in hybrid SUV, so the procurement case is different from both a pure EV and a conventional petrol SUV. Its electric range and fuel-efficiency claims depend on the test cycle, battery state of charge, route, climate, payload and how often the vehicle is plugged in. For a buyer with reliable home, depot or workplace charging, the PHEV system can reduce fuel use on regular short trips while keeping petrol range for longer routes. For a fleet that rarely charges, the headline EV range becomes much less relevant. Before buying, check local electricity supply, plug type, charging power, fuel grade, workshop capability and how the vehicle will be driven in real service. Older or regional stock can be materially different Visually similar SONG PLUS DM-i vehicles should not be assumed to share the same technical package. An older official BYD Brazil MY23 sheet, for example, listed an 8.3 kWh battery and different power figures. That historical document is not a current global specification, but it is important evidence for used-car and old-stock buyers: the badge alone does not tell you the battery or powertrain version. If a supplier offers a discounted or used unit, ask for a dated specification sheet and photos of the VIN plate, charging inlet, engine compartment, battery labels and instrument information. This is more reliable than copying specifications from the newest version found online. Safety ratings must match the actual vehicle identity ANCAP publishes a safety rating for the BYD SEALION 6 PHEV sold in Australia and New Zealand. ANCAP explains that the rating applies to those PHEV variants and was supported by additional PHEV crash testing. That is useful safety evidence for the vehicle family, but it should not automatically be attached to every SONG PLUS DM-i sold in another market. Warranty, parts and connected functions can depend on the sales channel After-sales support is not a minor detail on a modern PHEV. In a June 2025 statement covering several Caribbean markets, BYD said that only customers purchasing through its authorised distributor are guaranteed manufacturer warranty, genuine parts/accessories and certified servicing in those named markets. BYD also warned that non-official purchases may lose certain connected functions such as app connectivity, OTA updates or infotainment features. What to verify before paying a deposit A serious quotation should identify the exact vehicle, not just “SONG PLUS DM-i 2026.” Before payment, match the VIN to the vehicle, official market specification and commercial documents. Who is the SONG PLUS DM-i a sensible export choice for? The model can make sense for buyers who want a five-seat SUV with a plug-in hybrid powertrain and who operate in markets where both petrol supply and regular charging are practical. It can also suit dealers that need an alternative between a full EV and a conventional ICE SUV. Frequently asked questions Safety ratings must match the actual vehicle identity For an export order, verify the body code, production range, restraint equipment and destination approval separately.
